items.headline: Oregon elementary school shooting kills 3 children and a teacher
items.summary: Police say three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher were killed in a shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday. TIME's explainer outlines what is known about the attack.

items.headline: Trump cancels livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution
items.summary: President Trump called off plans to livestream the firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. The reversal followed criticism from members of both parties.

items.headline: Ukraine resumes energy strikes as Trump-Zelenskyy rift deepens
items.summary: Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian energy targets, saying Russia never stopped its own attacks, as tensions between Trump and Zelenskyy worsened. Ukrainian forces also say reduced access to SpaceX's Starshield military satellite service has hurt battlefield operations.

items.headline: Drone strikes ship in Romanian waters
items.summary: Romania began search and rescue operations in the Black Sea after a drone hit a ship that caught fire. The attack has added to fears that Russia's war in Ukraine is spreading.

items.headline: Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports and oil sites
items.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels have pledged to keep attacking Saudi Arabia's airports and oil facilities. The Nation's David Faris argues the Iran war's move into a Saudi phase signals more escalation.

items.headline: Suspicious mailings sent to election and congressional offices
items.summary: The FBI and the Postal Inspection Service are investigating mailings sent to election and congressional offices in several states. Some of the envelopes contained an unidentified white powder.

items.headline: Poll finds voters frustrated with Trump want major change
items.summary: An AP-NORC poll finds most voters think Trump is underperforming on domestic and foreign issues and want major change in the midterms. In an NPR focus group, several young Trump voters said they regret their 2024 vote.

items.headline: September retail sales rise 0.8%, lifted by gas spending
items.summary: Retail sales rose 0.8% in September, but only 0.2% excluding gas stations. The figures are not adjusted for inflation, which sped up last month.

items.headline: Appeals court to weigh who owns presidential records
items.summary: A federal appeals court will hear the administration's argument that White House records belong to Trump personally rather than to the public. The dispute could reach the Supreme Court.

items.headline: Santa Ana winds bring wildfire warnings to Southern California
items.summary: The season's first Santa Ana winds triggered red flag fire warnings in parts of Southern California. Possible power shutoffs were also flagged for some areas.

digest.overview:
A shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, killed three children and a teacher on Thursday, police said. President Trump dropped plans to livestream the firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan after bipartisan criticism. Federal investigators are examining mailings, some containing white powder, sent to election and congressional offices in several states. September retail sales rose 0.8%, or 0.2% excluding gas stations, and producer prices jumped 1.3% from August. An AP-NORC poll found most voters want major change in the midterms. A federal judge blocked sanctions on two U.S. groups that support the International Criminal Court. An appeals court will weigh whether White House records belong to Trump personally. Santa Ana winds brought red flag fire warnings to Southern California.

Abroad, Russian drone swarms on Kyiv and Kharkiv killed at least nine civilians and cut power to hundreds of thousands, as Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian energy sites. Seven sailors were reported missing after a drone hit a tanker in Romania's Black Sea waters. A Saudi diplomat accused Iran of encouraging Houthi attacks on the kingdom, and the EU postponed a summit with Gulf states. The World Food Programme said about 800,000 people in Yemen are cut off from aid. North Korea said it tested submarine-launched cruise missiles, apparently from a converted submarine for the first time. Sally Rooney's U.K. publisher stopped supplying her books over her support for the banned group Palestine Action. FIFA's Gianni Infantino apologized to the FIFA Council for errors in a World Cup investment plan. Yale e360 reported that governments are cutting Arctic wildlife research as security and mineral interests take priority.

home.overview:
The Brewers are headed to their first World Series since 1982 after a 6–4 win in Los Angeles completed a four-game NLCS sweep and ended the Dodgers' three-peat bid; Jake Bauers was named series MVP, and Shohei Ohtani's three-run homer wasn't enough. In the ALCS, rookie Petey Halpin's two-run homer lifted Cleveland past Tampa Bay 3–2 for a 2–1 lead, with Game 4 tonight if the rain holds off. In the NFL, Wil Lutz's 53-yard overtime field goal gave Denver a 17–14 win over Seattle after two late Sam Darnold interceptions. Jalen Hurts is out Sunday with a blood clot, and the weekend brings Chargers-Chiefs and Cowboys-Packers. NBA opening night is Tuesday.

Milan won 4–0 at Salzburg behind an Alphadjo Cisse hat-trick and Leverkusen won 4–0 at Lech Poznań, while Juventus lead the Europa League after a 2–1 win at Celta and Lyon beat Crystal Palace 3–2. Brighton opened their Conference League run by beating Kauno Žalgiris 4–0. Liverpool are sweating on Isak, Gakpo and Szoboszlai before visiting Brentford, Burnley host Wolves tonight, and Saturday brings Real Betis vs Barcelona and Bayern vs RB Leipzig. In the KBO, Kia's James Naile faces LG's Anders Tolhurst as the first round opens Saturday in Gwangju.

brief: Kia and LG open their best-of-five first round Saturday at 2 p.m. KST in Gwangju, renewing a postseason rivalry for the first time in a decade.
Kia will start James Naile (13-7, 3.49 ERA), and LG counters with Anders Tolhurst (12-11, 4.24), who went 1-3 with a 6.20 ERA in five starts against Kia this year.
LG closer Son Ju-young, who missed the wild card game with a neck injury, is expected to travel to Gwangju, but second baseman Shin Min-jae is unlikely to play.
Games 3 and 4 move to Jamsil on Oct. 20–21, and the series winner faces No. 2 Samsung in the second round.

brief: The Brewers beat the Dodgers 6–4 in Los Angeles to complete a four-game NLCS sweep and reach their first World Series since 1982, with Jake Bauers named NLCS MVP.

Garrett Mitchell's go-ahead leadoff homer in the sixth and David Hamilton's ninth-inning shot off Edwin Díaz backed Aaron Ashby's three-inning save, after Shohei Ohtani's three-run homer had put Los Angeles up 4–0.
Rookie Petey Halpin's two-run homer in the fifth lifted the Guardians past the Rays 3–2 in ALCS Game 3 for a 2–1 series lead, as Gavin Williams struck out nine in five innings.
ALCS Game 4 is tonight in Cleveland with Nick Martinez starting for Tampa Bay and more rain in the forecast, and the World Series opens Friday, Oct. 23.
Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas announced his retirement after 13 seasons.
